winning_patterns: Short 13-15 second clips with high-energy streamer reactions outperform longer 30 second clips by a 2.4x median view margin
Hooks that promise a specific failure or broken mechanic (crashing, physics, painting) generate significantly higher YouTube views than generic scene descriptions
Clips featuring ohnepixel and xQc dominate top views, indicating that established streamer brand recognition drives initial click-through more than the specific in-game event
avoid_patterns: Reject 30 second clips with slow buildup and no immediate payoff, as seen in the 1 view GTA-012 flop
Avoid generic location-based hooks like strip club scenes that lack a conflict, mistake, or streamer reaction
Do not post clips with zero likes, shares, or comments as they indicate zero audience resonance and algorithmic death
hook_style_guidance: Write Frame-1 hooks that state a specific broken promise, glitch, or mistake in all caps to create immediate curiosity and conflict within the first second.
